newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea hits back at U.S. over human rights.
newsitem.headline: North Korea hits back at U.S. over human rights.

text.p: North Korea hit back at Washington on Thursday for listing the communist country as a prominent violator of human rights by saying that the United States has the worst human rights record in the world.
"Admittedly, it is the United States that has the most serious human rights problem in the world," a spokesman for the North Korean Foreign Ministry said.
In its 20th annual report on human rights, the U.S. State Department said last week that North Korea was among Asian countries which committed serious human rights abuses last year.
As it does annually, the report faulted North Korea in every category, saying the Stalinist government in Pyongyang "continues to deny its citizens human rights."

"It is strikingly clear that their charging other nations with the 'human rights problem' is only a word-juggling ignoring the U.S. situation of human rights and a political plot seeking double standards in the issue of human rights," the North Korean spokesman said.
His statement was carried by the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) monitored in Tokyo.
"The U.S. slander against the DPRK (North Korea) is part of its reckless pressure prompted by its hostile policy towards the DPRK," he said.

"Korean socialism, which regards the juche (self-reliance) idea as its political philosophy, centred on the masses of the people, is the best social system in the world which perfectly guarantees their human rights," he said.
In China, a state-sponsored group of Chinese academics also slammed the U.S. report which criticises Beijing for silencing dissent.
The academics condemned the report as a malicious and slanderous interference in China's internal affairs, official media said on Thursday.

The report had violated the principles of the United Nations and ignored the progress China had made in protecting human rights, the official People's Daily quoted the scholars as concluding at a seminar in Beijing.
Vietnam on Wednesday also dismissed the U.S. State Department report on human rights and it, too, accused Washington of hundreds of years of abuses of its own.

A lengthy commentary in the Communist Party's Nhan Dan newspaper said the State Department's annual report, issued last week, was using human rights as an outdated pretext for interference in the internal affairs of Asian nations.
Indonesia also lashed out at the U.S. report on Wednesday, saying much of it was exaggerated.

The report said Indonesia continued to commit serious human rights abuses in 1996, including in East Timor, where it cited killings, disappearances, tortue and excessive use of force by the military and insurgents.
